key: Two people each holding a deck of cards
name: ch10_card_decks_merge_join
alt: Two friends lay down number-sorted card decks side by side, pairing matching top cards, while an inset shows an unsorted deck silently missing a match.
scene: Two friends sit facing each other on a durrie on a verandah floor, seen from slightly above, with no table between them, only a narrow strip of floor where cards are laid down. On the left, a young woman in a green salwar kurta holds a deck of playing cards sorted by number, face up, the top card showing a large 7. On the right, a young man in a striped half-sleeve shirt and spectacles holds his own sorted deck, the top card also showing 7. Between them, the two sevens are being placed together as a neat pair with a small green tick, and behind it a short row of earlier pairs (3 with 3, 5 with 5) lies in order. A curved arrow shows the man about to put down a lone 6 on his side and move on, because 6 is smaller than the woman's next card, an 8. Both look relaxed, cards held close, nothing spread out. In a small inset bubble at the bottom right, the same pair hold decks that are not sorted: the woman's deck shows 9 on top with a 4 buried below, and a hidden matching 4 slides past unnoticed in the man's pile, marked with a small red cross and a question mark, neither of them noticing. Warm late-afternoon light, a potted tulsi plant and a steel tumbler of tea on the floor nearby. Labels: "MERGE" above the row of matched pairs, and "UNSORTED" above the inset bubble.

key: A government file system with a rule
name: ch10_govt_file_record_room
alt: In a government office every file is stamped, photocopied and stored in a record room between desks, a nicer form does not speed it up, and only a new rule lets files pass directly.
scene: A wide cut-away view of an old Indian government office corridor with three wooden desks in a row from left to right, each with a clerk in a white shirt or sari, ceiling fans turning and tall steel almirahs along the back wall. Between every two desks there is a small record room with an open grille door: a peon in a khaki uniform carries a buff-coloured file tied with red tape from the first desk into the record room, where it is stamped with a big rubber stamp, photocopied on a bulky machine and the copy shelved, and only then carried out to the next desk; looping arrows show this detour repeating between each pair of desks, and a wall clock shows the hours slipping by. The clerks wait with chins on their hands; one desk has a new clerk arriving with a transfer order while the old one leaves, yet the file is safe on the record room shelf. In the foreground, a citizen holds a neat new printed form with tidy boxes, smiling, but the file still follows the same slow detour. In a small inset at the top right, a notice on the wall shows a new rule, and the file passes straight from desk to desk on a short arrow while the record room door stays shut. Dusty afternoon light through tall windows. Labels: "RECORD ROOM" above the first record room door, and "NEW ENGINE" above the top-right inset.
